---
title: "Python"
---

The Python below is static code. The SQL inside it is the same SQL you can run
in your browser: press **Run** to see what it returns against the latest
release.

## Install

```sh
pip install duckdb
```

## Attach and query

```python
import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("ATTACH 'https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/cancerbasemap.duckdb' AS cbm (READ_ONLY)")
```

Mammography screening in Colorado counties, lowest first, with the interval,
the release that said so, and the county's rurality code:

```{.sql .runnable}
SELECT u.name, o.source_release, o.value AS pct, o.lower, o.upper, o.value_status,
       r.value AS rucc_code
FROM measure.observation o
JOIN geography.unit u
  ON u.geo_id = o.geo_id AND u.vintage = 2026
LEFT JOIN measure.observation r
  ON r.geo_id = o.geo_id AND r.source = 'RUCC' AND r.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'
WHERE o.source = 'PLACES' AND o.measure_id = 'PLACES:MAMMOUSE:age_adjusted'
  AND o.source_release = '2025'
  AND o.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%' AND u.parent_geo_id = 'state:08'
ORDER BY pct LIMIT 10
```

In Python, run it against the `cbm` alias (`cbm.measure.observation`,
`cbm.geography.unit`) with `con.sql(...)`:

```python
con.sql("""
    SELECT u.name, o.source_release, o.value AS pct, o.lower, o.upper, o.value_status,
           r.value AS rucc_code
    FROM cbm.measure.observation o
    JOIN cbm.geography.unit u
      ON u.geo_id = o.geo_id AND u.vintage = 2026
    LEFT JOIN cbm.measure.observation r
      ON r.geo_id = o.geo_id AND r.source = 'RUCC' AND r.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'
    WHERE o.source = 'PLACES' AND o.measure_id = 'PLACES:MAMMOUSE:age_adjusted'
      AND o.source_release = '2025'
      AND o.geo_id LIKE 'county:08%' AND u.parent_geo_id = 'state:08'
    ORDER BY pct LIMIT 10
""").df()
```

`measure.observation` is laid out by state, so the `geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'`
filter (`08` is Colorado) lets DuckDB read just that state's part of it.

Fetch with `duckdb`, `requests` or `polars`: Python's default `urllib` user
agent is blocked by the zone (HTTP 403, Cloudflare error 1010). Pin a dated
folder (`.../data/v2026-11-02/cancerbasemap.duckdb`) for anything you will
rerun.

`u.vintage = 2026` is named explicitly rather than trusting `o.geo_vintage`
— see [Concepts › Time axes](/concepts/time-axes.qmd) for why a measure's own
`geo_vintage` column isn't always the vintage its `geo_id` actually belongs
to (tracked as [#21](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-basemap/issues/21)).

`con.sql(...)` returns a DuckDB relation; `.df()` materializes it as a
pandas `DataFrame`, `.arrow()` as an Arrow table, or iterate it directly —
whatever the rest of your analysis expects.
